items.text: Actor Rami Malek is going to play the villain in the newest ‘James Bond’ movie, and he is in final negotiations for the role. The news came after his win at the 2019 Oscars. He will join a list of famous Bond baddies such as Scaramanga and Silva. The 25 th Bond movie in the franchise is called ‘Shatterhands’. Cary Joi Fukunaga is the director and the filming will begin in April 2019. Daniel Craig will play Bond for the last time, and other familiar and famous actors will join him. Difficult words: villain (the ‘bad guy’), negotiation (a discussion to reach an agreement through compromise), baddie (slang for ‘bad guy’), franchise (a series of movies, shows, or restaurants or other things that are part of the same group or idea). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Actor Rami Malek is going to be the villain in the newest ‘James Bond’ movie. He is in final negotiations for the role. The news came after he won Best Actor at the 2019 Oscars. He will join a list of famous Bond bad guys. The 25 th Bond movie in the popular series is called ‘Shatterhands’. The filming will start in April. Daniel Craig will play Bond for the last time. Difficult words: villain (the ‘bad guy’ of the story), negotiation (talking together to come to an agreement). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

‘James Bond’ movies are popular. There are 24 of these movies. People are planning the 25 th movie. Its name is ‘Shatterhands’. Daniel Craig is going to play James Bond. Rami Malek is going to be the villain . Malek recently won an Oscar for Best Actor . Difficult words: villain (the ‘bad guy’ of the story), won (past of ‘win’), Best Actor (the Oscar Award for a male actor in a movie). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The historic meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un took place in Vietnam’s capital of Hanoi last week. The centre of the summit was a denuclearisation between the two countries. However, the talks ended earlier than planned, and people cancelled the signing ceremony. President Trump explained his decision to walk away from the denuclearisation deal in a press conference. He said that North Korea was willing to denuke a large portion of the areas that the USA wanted it to, but North Korea wanted all of its sanctions lifted for that, and the USA could not do this. Nevertheless, Trump said that the countries conducted the talks in a constructive and friendly manner and that work and talks between them will continue. Difficult words: summit (a meeting), denuke (short for denuclearise – get rid of nuclear weapons), sanctions (putting limits to what a country can and cannot do), lift (end, stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a historic meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un last week, and they met in Vietnam’s capital of Hanoi. They were there to talk about the denuclearisation of North Korea. The meeting ended earlier than planned, and they did not sign a deal . Trump later explained why he walked away from the talks. He said that North Korea wanted to denuclearise a large area, which is what the USA wanted, but North Korea wanted USA to stop all the sanctions for that. The USA did not want to do that, so the meeting ended. Trump said that the two days of talks were interesting, productive and friendly. The talks between the two countries will continue. Difficult words: denuclearisation (putting away nuclear weapons – bombs and rockets), sign a deal (say ‘yes’ to an official document), denuclearise (put away nuclear weapons), sanctions (limits to what a country can or cannot do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

North Korea has nuclear weapons . The USA does not like this. The USA wants North Korea to get rid of its nuclear weapons. The USA puts sanctions on North Korea. North Korea does not like this. This is a difficult situation. The leaders of the countries meet. Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un talk about it. They meet in Vietnam. They talk for two days. North Korea can get rid of many nuclear weapons. To do this, North Korea wants all of the sanctions to stop. The USA does not want to stop all of them. Nothing comes from the talks. Nothing is bad, and nothing is good. Difficult words: nuclear weapons (bomb and rockets which can destroy cities and countries), get rid (put away), sanctions (rules on what a country can or cannot do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A year ago at the same time of this year, Britain was facing the ’Beast from the East’ – a period of cold weather when temperatures dropped to -8.9° Celsius in parts of the south. The cold brought widespread disruption and even froze the fountains in Trafalgar Square. However, last week saw Londoners having picnics in the parks with a day as high as 21.2° Celsius last Monday. The day was the UK’s warmest February day on record, beating the previous record of 19.7° Celsius from 1998. It remains to be seen what kind of weather this summer will bring. Difficult words: disruption (when there is a problem with something and it is not working normally), remains to be seen (it is not yet known). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last February, it was very cold in Britain when the temperature dropped to -8.9° Celsius in the southern parts of the country. The cold brought disruptions and it even froze famous fountains in London. However, last week was quite the opposite of that, as last Monday was the warmest February day on record. The temperature was as high as 21.2° Celsius. Difficult words: disruption (a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last February in Britain, it was very cold. It was around -8.9° Celsius. That was very cold for Britain. There were problems. This February is different. Last Monday was the warmest February day ever. It was 21.2° Celsius! Difficult words: was (past of ‘is’), were (past of ‘are’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Richard Branson is hosting a concert in a Colombian border town to support people in Venezuela. People hope that soon it will be possible to get supplies there so that people are not suffering so much. The Venezuela regime is pushing strongly against protesters, which has led to violent clashes. Despite the violence, thousands crossed the border to attend the concert. People expect that a total of 250,000 people will attend. Over 30 renowned Latin American artists are performing at the event. They hope to raise an ambitious 100 million dollars. Difficult words: supplies (food, clothes and other things necessary for daily life), despite (opposite to). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Richard Branson is hosting a concert in a Colombian border town to support people in Venezuela. People hope that soon it will be possible to get food and clothing into Venezuela so that the people’s lives there are not so difficult. The regime in Venezuela is pushing strongly against protesters and there is violence in the streets. Thousands of people crossed the border to go to the concert. People expect there will be 250,000 people at the concert. Over 30 famous Latin American singers will be there, and they hope to get 100 million dollars for the Venezuelan people. Difficult words: host (introduce artists at a concert), regime (a government which controls people very strongly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a concert in Colombia. It is near Venezuela. The concert is for the Venzeulean people. The singers want to help the people. They want to bring food and clothing to Venezuela. People there do not have easy lives. This is the reason why some people do not like the Venezuelan government . They fight in the streets. Thousands of people go to the concert. People think that there are 250,000 people at the concert. 30 Latin American singers sing at the concert. They want to get 100 million dollars for people in Venezuela. Difficult words: reason (why something is), government (the bosses of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People rescued sixteen stranded passengers from a ride at SeaWorld in San Diego. They were stuck in gondolas for several hours, and it was already night when help came. The rescuers took them down one by one. A strong wind caused the problem which broke the machines which controls the electricity. Difficult words: stranded (when you cannot get out of a place without help), stuck (stopped and not being able to move). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People rescued sixteen passengers from gondolas in San Diego. The passengers had to wait for several hours and it was night when the help came. Rescuers took them down one-by-one. A strong wind caused the problem which broke the machine which controls the electricity. Difficult words: rescue (save), cause (the reason for something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sixteen people need help in San Diego. They are in gondolas . The gondolas stop. The people have to wait for many hours. It is night when help comes. The people come down from gondolas very slowly. The gondolas stop because a strong wind breaks the machine which controls the electricity. Difficult words: gondola (a small room on a cable), have to (must). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Seventeen people died after a fire broke out at a hotel in central New Delhi. The hotel is a five-story building, and firefighters felt forced to use windows in their rescue attempts. Officials are yet to determine the cause of the devastating fire. Difficult words: break out (start), determine (find out the facts about something), cause (the reason or reasons as to why something happened). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Seventeen people died after a fire started at a hotel in central New Delhi. The hotel is a five-floor building, and firefighters had to use windows when they tried to rescue people. The police now need to find out what started the horrible fire. Difficult words: rescue (save), find out (find information). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Seventeen people die in a fire. The fire starts at a hotel. The hotel is in central New Delhi. The hotel has five floors. Firefighters must use the windows to try to help the people. Now, the police need to work. They need to understand the reason for the fire. Difficult words: firefighter (a person who stops a fire), reason (why something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Caster Semenya is a female athlete from South Africa, and she has taken the International Association of Athletics Federation (IAAF) to court because it wants to force her to take medication to lower her testosterone . The secretary for the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) said that the hearing will take one week which is unusually long. People questioned Semenya’s gender as a woman after she won the World Championship in 2009, and the IAAF wants to ensure that all female athletes have similar testosterone levels. The IAAF president said that the rules are there to help female athletes have fair competitions. The court will decide Semenya’s future as an athlete and others like her next month. Difficult words: testosterone (a chemical in the body that all people have, but men have more of it than women; testosterone helps you be strong and fast); hearing (when people go to a court so the law can help them make a decision), gender (males or females). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Caster Semenya is an athlete from South Africa who is taking an athletics organisation to court. The organisation wants to force the woman to take medication to lower her testosterone . A man who is working at the court said that the decision will be made after one week. People were not sure if Semenya was a woman after she won a competition in 2009. The organisation wants to be sure that all female athletes have similar amounts of testosterone. The organisation’s president said that the rules are there to help female athletes compete equally. Difficult words: testosterone (a chemical in the body which all people have, but men have more of it than women; testosterone helps you be strong); amount (how much of something you have), compete (try to win against other people in sport). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Caster Semenya is a woman from South Africa. She is an athlete. She is going to court . An organisation for athletes wants to give her medicine. She does not want to take this medicine. The medicine can make her testosterone go down. In 2009, Caster wins a big race. People say that they are not sure if she is a woman or a man. The organisation wants similar levels of testosterone for all women. The organisation’s president says that the sports need rules. Then they are fair for everybody. Difficult words: court (a house where a judge works), testosterone (a chemical in all people’s bodies; men have more testosterone than women; testosterone helps you be strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel launched a small probe to the moon on a Falcon 9 SpaceX rocket. An engineer from the Israel Aerospace Industries said that it was going to be a difficult and long journey. There are quicker ways to get to the moon, but you need a powerful rocket for that (which Israel does not have). It will take the probe about 1,5 months to get to the moon. The lander weighs just 585 kilograms, and it will take advantage of gravitational forces to enter the moon’s orbit . The team received a message of good luck from space veteran Buzz Aldrin, a man who walked on the moon. The ’Beresheet’ robotic craft, named after the Hebrew word for Genesis, is expected to land on the moon on 11 April. The mission hopes to inspire students into STEM subjects. Difficult words: probe (a small thing which goes to space without any people inside), orbit (the area around the moon), STEM (a category of subjects at school – science, technology, engineering and mathematics). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Israel launched a small space craft to the moon on a Falcon 9 SpaceX rocket. The journey to the moon will be long – it will take 1,5 months. There is a quicker way to get to the moon, but Israel does not have a big enough rocket for that. This spacecraft is unmanned , and it is only 585 kilograms heavy. It is going to land on the moon on 11 April. The mission hopes to inspire students into STEM subjects. Difficult words: launch (send up), unmanned (without people inside), STEM (certain subjects at school – science, technology, engineering and mathematics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel is flying to the moon. It uses a Falcon 9 SpaceX rocket. This is not a very big rocket. The trip will take long. It will take 1,5 months. The probe will go to the moon on 11 April. It is small. It is only 585 kilograms heavy. It is just a machine. No one is inside it. Israel does this to inspire young people. They want more people to study science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Difficult words: will (in the future), probe (a machine which people send to space and has no people in it), engineering (designing, making machines and things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An African-American, openly gay actor named Jussie Smollett staged a fake homophobic attack on himself to make himself more popular, Chicago police said. The show business drama began when the 36-year-old said that two men attacked him in Chicago on the 29th of January. He said that the men shouted racist and homophobic slurs , tied a rope around his neck and poured chemicals on him. The attack shocked the public, celebrity friends and even US senators, and everyone came to the actor’s defence. However, the police soon found inconsistencies in Smollett’s story and their work changed. The men who attacked him said that they were paid by the actor, and the police concluded that the actor staged the attack. Now he is in trouble, and he could go to prison for up to three years. Difficult words: stage (organise something to happen), slur (saying something which make the person feel very bad), inconsistency (when things are inconsistent, they do not make sense and the story cannot be true). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An openly gay, African-American actor reported an attack on his person in January. He said that two men shouted racist and anti-gay slurs at him, put a rope around his neck, and poured chemicals on him. The attack shocked a lot of people. Celebrity friends and even US senators commented on the attack and said that it was terrible. The police started to investigate the attack. Things turned out differently than everyone thought. Police found out that the actor staged the attack, and the two men were paid by him. The actor is now in trouble, and he could go to prison for up to three years. Difficult words: slur (saying something which make the person feel very bad), investigate (try to find out what really happened), stage (organise, fake). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens in the USA. An actor says that two men attack him. He is African American and gay. He says that the men say racist and anti-gay things to him. They make him feel very bad. They put chemicals on him. They put a rope around his neck. The actor tells this to people and to police. Everyone is shocked. Police investigate . They see that the actor’s story is not right. They find out that he is lying. The actor organises everything. He gives money to the two men to attack him. He does this to get more popular. He is in trouble now. He can go to prison for three years. Difficult words: racist (against a group of people), rope (a long thing which people put around somebody’s neck to hang them – kill them), investigate (get more information and understand something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hundreds of people demonstrated against the government in Port-au-Prince in Haiti, and looters took control of the city’s business district . They set vehicles and a petrol station on fire. The police responded by firing tear gas and live shots, and they made several arrests. People are angry because inflation is extremely high there. The demonstrators are saying that President Jovenel Moise is corrupt, and they are asking him to quit. A court also said that officials took loans for themselves which were for the country. Difficult words: looter (a person who breaks and steals things because they are angry and poor), district (an area, a part), loan (money which you can use, but you have to pay back later). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People demonstrated against the government in the capital of Haiti. People also destroyed and robbed shops in the city’s business area. They set cars and a petrol station on fire. The police fought the protesters and arrested some of them. The people are angry because inflation is extremely high. People are saying that their president is corrupt , and they want him to quit. Haiti was going to get some money for help, but the corrupt officials took it for themselves. Difficult words: inflation (when you can buy less and less things for the same amount of money), corrupt (not doing their job – helping the country – but using their power to get rich), official (a person in a position of power, a boss of a country or a part of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Haiti protest. Some people break things. Some people set cars on fire. They set a petrol station on fire. Police fight the protesters. The people are angry. Inflation in Haiti is very high. They say that their president and the politicians are corrupt . They do not help the country. They only get money for themselves. Difficult words: inflation (when you can buy less and less things for the same amount of money), politician (a person in politics, a ‘boss’ of a country or city), corrupt (only taking money for themselves and not helping the country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, Donald Trump signed a new order at the White House. He said to be thrilled about this move leading towards creating the United States Space Force. Trump said that his administration recognised space as a war-fighting territory and made the creation of the Space Force a national security priority. He believes that it will receive great support from congress because of its importance. He said that the adversaries of the USA are taking the same steps, and space is going to be a very big part of the US defence and offence . However, according to him, there will be nobody who could come close to matching the USA, meaning that the nation’s safety is secured for many decades and generations. Difficult words: adversary (an opponent), defence (defending – protecting), offence (attacking). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Donald Trump signed a new order last week, and it is a step to create the United States Space Force . Trump said that he sees space as a war-fighting territory of the future. He believes that congress will support his order because it is important. He said that other countries are taking the same steps, but the American space technology is much better. Trump said that this means that the USA will be safe for a long time. Difficult words: sign (write down your name to show that you say ‘yes’ to something), order (a rule, an instruction – telling somebody what to do), force (war machines). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump orders something new. He wants to build the United States Space Force . He thinks the government can say ‘yes’ to this. Trump says that space is a place for future wars. He says that other countries are building space war machines, too. Donald Trump says that the American space force is the best. Other countries have worse war space machines. Thanks to this, America will be safe in the future. Difficult words: order (tell the people around him to do something), force (war machines), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lightsabre duelling could be seen only in Star Wars films, but the French Fencing Federation recently made it an official sport in the country. The lightsabre replicas are harmless , but they can look and sound just like the weapons in the movies. A lightsabre manufacturer said that it makes very basic ones, which only have an on-off button, and come in different colours or shapes. The more expensive versions include sound and blade effects. During battle, the Jedis or Siths can earn five points for a blow to the opponent’s head, three for striking the arms and legs and one point for hitting the hands. The winner is the person who reaches fifteen points first. Difficult words: harmless (it cannot harm/hurt/injure anybody), Jedi and Sith (the characters from the Star Wars films), blow noun (a hit, a strike). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Until now, you could only see lightsabre duels in the Star Wars films, but thanks to the French Fencing Federation, the activity became an official sport in the country. The fighters use fake lightsabres which cannot hurt anyone. The cheap ones only glow , but the more expensive versions have sound and light effects. The rules of lightsabre fencing are easy – a hit to the head is five points, a hit to the arms and legs is three, and a hit to the hands is one point. The winner is the person who reaches fifteen points first. Difficult words: lightsabre (a type of sabre/a sword in the sci-fi films Star Wars), fencing (a type of sport when people fight with swords), glow (give out light). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A lot of people know the Star Wars films. They are science fiction films. Many things in these films do not exist. Lightsabres are a type of sabres in the films. People make fake lightsabres for real life. They glow with light. Some make sounds and light effects. When two people fight, they call it a duel. Duelling with lightsabres becomes a sport in France. People can hit the opponent in a few areas. They can hit the head. They can hit the arms. They can hit the legs. Or they can hit the hand. If you hit your opponent, you get points. When you get 15 points, you win. Difficult words: sabre (=sword, a type of a weapon which is like a big long knife), glow (give out light), opponent (the person which you fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fashion icon Karl Lagerfeld died at the age of 85. He was the creative director of Chanel, and he was a legend who continued working until his last days. He had been unwell for a number of weeks, and he missed Chanel’s culture show in Paris last month. Born in 1933, he spent an impressive 36 years working at the fashion house and he was well known for this signature suited look. Difficult words: impressive (so many that you think that it is special), signature (typical for him). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Karl Lagerfeld was born in 1933, and he worked for Chanel as the creative director for 36 years. He was a fashion icon . He always wore similar clothing – a shirt, suit, tie and black glasses. This became his typical look . Last month, he missed Chanel’s culture show. He was not well and recently he died. He was 85. Difficult words: creative director (the most important person in the company; he made new clothes, told other people what to do), icon (a person who is respected), look noun (the way he dresses – what he wears). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about Karl Lagerfeld. He works for Chanel. Chanel is a fashion company . He is the most important person in Chanel. He works there for 36 years. He becomes a fashion icon . Now Karl Lagerfeld is old. He is 85. He becomes unwell . He dies. Difficult words: company (a business), icon (a person who is respected), unwell (ill). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Yellow vest protests have taken place in Paris for the 14th consecutive weekend. A small group of them shouted anti-Semitic insults at a 69-year-old Jewish philosopher. The police later arrived in the video to protect the man from possible violence. In the Parisian city centre, police used tear gas to break up thousands of protesters. The French president said that these situations are the absolute opposite of what makes France great. Difficult words: consecutive (following one after another), anti-Semitic (anti-Jewish), insult (saying something which makes the person feel very bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Yellow vests are a group of people who are protesting in France, and they have a protest every weekend. This weekend was the 14th protest. A small group of protesters shouted anti-Semitic insults at a man. He is a 69-year-old Jewish philosopher, and the police came to protect him from possible violence . In the centre of Paris, thousands of people protested. Police broke them up. The French president said that things like this are the opposite of what makes France great. Difficult words: anti-Semitic (anti-Jewish), insult (saying something which makes the person feel very bad), violence (attacking, hitting the person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Paris. There are protests every weekend. This weekend is the 14th weekend of protests. A group of people called ‘yellow vests’ protest. This weekend, some of them see a man. He is a 69-year-old Jewish philosopher. They shout anti-Semitic insults at him. In the centre of Paris, thousands of people protest. The police stop them. The French president does not like this. Difficult words: shout (say very strongly and with a lot of bad emotions), anti-Semitic (anti-Jewish), insult (saying something which makes the person feel very bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, California’s Governor, Gavin Newsom, announced plans to withdraw all of the state’s National Guard troops from the border between Mexico and the USA. The 360 troops will be redeployed to fight fires and gather information on drug cartels. The governor thinks that Trump’s ‘border emergency’ is not real and he and California will not be a part of that political theatre. Political theatre is when a leader says things to get people to listen to him. The previous week, New Mexico’s governor made a similar decision – she withdrew most of her state’s National Guard members from the border. Difficult words: announce (officially say something), withdraw (leave a place), redeployed (deploy/put troops/soldiers somewhere else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

California is a state in the USA. Its southern border is with Mexico and there are 360 Californian troops at the border. Last week, California’s governor announced a plan. He wants to move all of the troops from the border to fight fires or look for information on drug cartels instead. The governor said that Trumps border crisis is not real, and that California will not be a part of his political theatre. Political theatre is when a leader says things to get people to want to follow him or her. Difficult words: troops (police or soldiers), announce (officially say something), crisis (a time of danger and problems). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

California is a state in the USA. Its southern border is with Mexico. California has 360 troops at the border. California wants to move the troops away. They will do something else. For example, they can fight fires. The Californian governor talks about this plan. He says that there is no problem at the border. He says that it is Trump’s political theatre. Political theatre is when a leader says things to get people to want to follow him or her. He does not want to be a part of his theatre. Difficult words: border (the line between two countries), troops (police or soldiers), governor (the boss of an American state). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A town on a remote island off the northern coast of Russia declared a state of emergency after a group of polar bears invaded it. Due to climate change, polar bears are forced into closer contact with humans – they look for food in rubbish dumps and enter homes and public buildings. People say that the invasion started because of melting ice in the Arctic which forces the bears to look for food on land. Difficult words: remote (far from a city), declare (formally say that something is true), rubbish dump (a place for things which people throw away). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A group of polar bears invaded a town in Russia when they were looking for food in rubbish dumps . They also entered homes and public buildings. The town, on an island north of continental Russia, said that this was an emergency as polar bears can be dangerous. People say that there is less and less Arctic ice, so the bears are moving south to look for food. Difficult words: invade (enter in large numbers and make problems), rubbish dump (a place for things which people throw away), emergency (a serious, dangerous situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Arctic ice is melting . This means that the polar bears cannot hunt . They are hungry. They move south to look for food. Many of them go to a Russian village. They look for food there. They look for it in rubbish dumps . They enter houses and buildings, too. Polar bears are big and strong. They can be dangerous. Difficult words: melt (turn from ice to water), hunt (catch other animals to eat; for example fish), rubbish dump (a place for things which people throw away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In southern India, a controversial bull- taming sport called Jallikattu is making a comeback. Thousands of people came to watch the tradition that is centuries old. India’s top court banned this tradition because of animal cruelty. One man said that people poke the bulls with sharp objects, force them to drink liquor, and jab or twist their tails. In 2017, the sport came back to the Tamil Nadu state after protests forced laws to change. PETA is campaigning for the ban of the sport to return. A man for the sport said that he wants PETA to be banned in Tamil Nadu because unlike Spain and other countries, he says that the people think of the bulls as their own children. Difficult words: tame (do things to an animal so that you can control it), jab (hit sharply and quickly), PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals – an organisation that protects animals). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In southern India, a controversial bull- taming sport is making a comeback. Thousands of people came to watch the tradition which is centuries old. India’s top court stopped this tradition because of animal cruelty . One man said that people hit the bulls with sharp objects, force them to drink alcohol, and hurt their tails. In 2017, the sport came back when protests made the laws change. An organisation wants the court to ban the sport again. A man who wants the sport said that people think of the bulls as their own children. Difficult words: controversial (when people feel strongly about something and they argue or talk about the thing), tame (do things to an animal so that you can control it), cruelty (being cruel – doing something that hurts the animal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In southern India, there is a bull- taming sport. It is controversial . It is very popular. It is very old. India’s leaders stop this sport for some time. The leaders say that the sport is cruel . One man says that people hit the bulls with sharp objects. They make them drink alcohol. They hurt their tails. In 2017, the sport comes back. This is after people protest. They change the laws. An organisation wants the leaders to stop the sport again. One man wants the sport. He says that people think of the bulls as their children. Difficult words: tame (do things to an animal so that you can control it), controversial (when people feel strongly about something and they argue or talk about the thing), cruel (very bad for the animals – they get hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At eight days old, doctors told baby Theo’s parents that he might not survive because his heart was improperly pumping blood. However, Theo defied the odds when he survived 25 cardiac arrests in just one day. He had two operations and a doctor said that it was amazing how quickly the baby recovered. Eighteen months later, Theo is still doing well and his parents are very proud of him. His mother said that he has ‘ a zest for life ’, and his father said that ‘he was kept on this earth to do something special’. On February 5 th , Lunar New Year began. This year is the Year of the Pig . In China, thousands of people celebrated it. Some performers re-enacted historical ceremonies, while people had family meetings and parties. Others burned the first joss sticks of the year to bring them good fortune. In North Korea, people celebrated the new year, too, although a bit differently. They laid wreaths at the statues of their leaders and bowed to them. North Koreans did not use to recognise Lunar New Year, but now it is a holiday there, too. However, North Koreans must pay their respects to the country’s leaders. In Singapore, people celebrated by having fireworks displays. Difficult words: Lunar New Year (the new year based on the cycle of the moon; it is celebrated in many Asian countries and cultures), Year of the Pig (the Chinese zodiac has twelve animals for twelve years, including the pig; a zodiac is an idea that there are different important symbols in the sky), joss sticks (sticks which smell when you burn them). Last November in California, there were several deadly wildfires that are now the most expensive in the state’s history. The insurance claims from the fires are at $11.4 billion. Just one of the fires in Paradise, California, killed the most people and destroyed the most buildings in California’s history. It killed 86 people, destroyed about 19,000 buildings, and it burnt about 153,000 acres of land. California’s insurance commissioner said that there are 46,000 claims from the other Californian wildfires, which completely destroyed 13,000 homes and businesses. The largest electric company in California is the Pacific Gas and Electric Company. In 2017, people say that the wind and its electric wiring may have started large fires, and the company has to pay a lot of money to fix the problems. In 2018, people say that its wiring starts some of the fires again. The company filed for bankruptcy . Difficult words: insurance claim (you pay money to an insurance company to get money in case an accident or a disaster happens to something that you own; an insurance claim is when you ask for that money such as after a fire or a flood), insurance commissioner (the person in charge of the insurance for the people in state), bankruptcy (when a company says that it is running out of money and must stop the business).
